headline: Dartmouth Health eliminates 124 positions and cancels 303 openings
dek: The New Hampshire health system says rising operating costs and slower, lower insurance payments drove a restructuring that also affects several programs.
body: Dartmouth Health eliminated 124 filled positions and canceled 303 open positions this week as the New Hampshire-based health system restructures operations, according to a Sept. 15 announcement.

The changes affect Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center and Dartmouth Hitchcock Clinics Southern Region. Dartmouth Health said operating expenses have grown 12% as labor, supply and drug costs rise while insurers pay less and take longer to pay.

The system said it is also ending or restructuring Tele-ICU and Tele-ED services, winding down the New England Alliance for Health as its members have joined larger systems, and outsourcing its Lean Six Sigma employee training programs. Leaders said they are working with affected facilities on alternative care plans for patients who use the telehealth services.

Dartmouth Health said the affected employees will receive transition resources and can pursue other roles within the system. The organization says it has more than 16,000 employees and includes eight member hospitals plus clinics across New Hampshire and Vermont.
author: NorthEast News Desk
